title: Drone Delivery Cost per Package: Industry Benchmarks vs. Project SkyNet Projections
executive_question: How does Project SkyNet's projected cost reduction compare to industry benchmarks over time?
required_metrics: Entity (e.g., Amazon Prime Air, Wing, Zipline, Project SkyNet projection)
comparison_set: Project SkyNet internal projections vs. published benchmarks from Amazon, Wing, Zipline, and industry reports (e.g., McKinsey, BCG).
preferred_sources: Company annual reports (Amazon, Alphabet/Wing, Zipline)
Industry reports (McKinsey 'Drone Delivery Economics', BCG 'Last-Mile Innovation')
Academic papers (e.g., Journal of Air Transport Management)
search_queries: Amazon Prime Air drone delivery cost per package 2023 2024 2025
Wing drone delivery cost per package benchmark 2024
Zipline drone delivery cost per package 2023 2024 2025
data_quality_rule: Only include publicly reported or estimated costs from credible sources. If only two data points exist, use CAGR to interpolate intermediate years and mark as estimates.
narrative_role: Validate the financial viability hypothesis (H1) by showing that the projected 35% cost reduction aligns with or outperforms industry trends.
pre_exhibit_context: The financial model assumes a 35% reduction in last-mile delivery costs by Q4 2027. We need to test this against real-world benchmarks.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Project SkyNet's cost trajectory is consistent with industry leaders, supporting the feasibility of the 18-month break-even target.

title: Consumer Acceptance of Drone Delivery: Global Survey Trends (2022-2026)
executive_question: Is the 68% consumer comfort level stable or declining, and how does it vary by region?
required_metrics: Percentage of consumers comfortable with drone delivery (%)
comparison_set: Global average vs. North America vs. Europe vs. Asia-Pacific.
preferred_sources: PwC 'Consumer Acceptance of Drones' reports
Deloitte 'Smart Mobility Consumer Survey'
McKinsey 'Last-Mile Delivery Consumer Insights'
search_queries: consumer acceptance drone delivery survey 2022 2023 2024 2025 2026
PwC drone delivery consumer comfort percentage 2024
Deloitte smart mobility drone delivery acceptance 2025
data_quality_rule: Use only surveys with sample sizes >1000 and published methodology. If annual data is missing, use linear interpolation with clear labeling.
narrative_role: Support H2 by showing that consumer acceptance is trending positively and that mitigation strategies can maintain high acceptance.
pre_exhibit_context: Our survey shows 68% comfort with drone delivery, but concerns about noise and privacy persist. We need to see if this is consistent globally.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Consumer acceptance is rising globally, and our mitigation measures (Whisper-Prop, camera shuttering) address the top concerns, making the 68% target sustainable.

title: Regulatory Milestones for Urban Drone Delivery: FAA/EASA Timeline (2020-2027)
executive_question: What are the key regulatory gates that Project SkyNet must pass, and are they on track?
required_metrics: Milestone (e.g., FAA Part 135 waiver, EASA UAM certification, local noise ordinance approval)
comparison_set: Project SkyNet planned milestones vs. actual regulatory developments.
preferred_sources: FAA press releases and regulatory dockets
EASA UAM framework publications
Local government ordinances (e.g., Los Angeles, New York, Chicago)
search_queries: FAA drone delivery Part 135 waiver timeline 2024 2025 2026
EASA UAM regulatory framework 2025 2026
urban drone delivery noise ordinance Los Angeles 2025
data_quality_rule: Only include official regulatory announcements or published timelines. Mark estimated dates with an asterisk.
narrative_role: Assess regulatory compliance (H3) by mapping required approvals against planned launch date.
pre_exhibit_context: Regulatory compliance is critical: altitude limits, restricted zones, weight limits, and data retention. We need to see if the timeline aligns with regulatory milestones.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Key regulatory milestones (e.g., FAA Part 135 waiver, EASA UAM framework) are achievable by Q4 2026, but the weight limit issue requires fleet mix adjustment.

title: Fleet Mix Comparison: Heavy-Lifter v2 vs. Swift-Class
executive_question: How do the two drone models compare on weight, payload, and compliance, and what is the impact on delivery capacity?
preferred_sources: Internal OmniLogistics drone specifications (from engineering team)
FAA weight limit regulations (14 CFR Part 107)
search_queries: Heavy-Lifter v2 drone specifications payload weight
Swift-Class drone specifications payload weight
FAA drone weight limit 25 lbs regulation
data_quality_rule: Use internal specs if publicly available; otherwise, request from engineering. Mark any estimated values.
narrative_role: Quantify the fleet readiness issue (H3) and the trade-off between using Heavy-Lifter v2 (non-compliant) vs. Swift-Class (compliant).
pre_exhibit_context: The Heavy-Lifter v2 exceeds the 25 lbs weight limit by 2.5 lbs, making it non-compliant. We need to compare its capabilities with the Swift-Class to assess operational impact.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Swift-Class is fully compliant but has lower payload capacity; shifting the fleet mix may reduce per-drone delivery volume, requiring more drones or longer operating hours.

title: Top 5 Urban Markets: Delivery Volume Potential (Packages per Day)
executive_question: Can the top 5 urban markets collectively support 150,000 packages/day?
required_metrics: City/Market (e.g., Los Angeles, New York, Chicago, Houston, Phoenix)
Source (e.g., USPS, FedEx, local demand study)
comparison_set: Each market's estimated volume vs. the target share (e.g., 30,000 per market).
preferred_sources: USPS package volume data by city
FedEx and UPS annual reports (city-level data if available)
Local economic development reports
search_queries: Los Angeles daily package delivery volume 2025
New York City last-mile delivery volume 2025
Chicago package delivery volume 2025
data_quality_rule: Use official postal or carrier data. If city-level data is unavailable, use metro area data and adjust by population share.
narrative_role: Test H5 by comparing market size estimates with the target volume.
pre_exhibit_context: The break-even target requires 150,000 packages/day across top 5 markets. We need to validate that each market has sufficient demand.
post_exhibit_takeaway: Markets A and B have high potential, but Markets D and E may fall short; a sixth market may be needed to reach the target.

title: Noise Pollution Standards and Drone Decibel Levels
executive_question: Do Whisper-Prop technology and other mitigations bring drone noise within acceptable urban limits?
required_metrics: Drone model (Heavy-Lifter v2, Swift-Class, with/without Whisper-Prop)
Regulatory limit (dB) (e.g., FAA, WHO, local ordinances)
comparison_set: Drone noise levels vs. regulatory limits vs. urban background noise.
preferred_sources: FAA noise standards (14 CFR Part 36)
WHO environmental noise guidelines
Local noise ordinances (e.g., Los Angeles Municipal Code)
Academic studies on drone noise (e.g., NASA, University of Southampton)
search_queries: FAA drone noise limit decibels 2025
WHO environmental noise guidelines 2024
drone noise decibel level Whisper-Prop technology
data_quality_rule: Use published decibel measurements from peer-reviewed studies or official test reports. If Whisper-Prop data is proprietary, request from engineering.
narrative_role: Support H2 by showing that noise mitigation brings decibel levels below regulatory and consumer thresholds.
pre_exhibit_context: Noise is the top consumer concern (42%). Whisper-Prop claims 40% reduction. We need to compare decibel levels against standards.
post_exhibit_takeaway: With Whisper-Prop, drone noise is below typical urban background noise and within FAA and WHO guidelines, alleviating the top concern.
